newsitem.title: JAPAN: Hitachi files patent complaint against Taiwan firm.
newsitem.headline: Hitachi files patent complaint against Taiwan firm.

text.p: Japan's Hitachi Ltd said on Wednesday that it had filed a complaint against Taiwanese semiconductor maker Winbond Electronics Corp and its U.S. unit with a U.S. District Court in New York for alleged patent infringement.

A company spokesman said Hitachi filed the complaint against Winbond and its wholly owned U.S. subsidiary Winbond Electronics North America Corp for alleged infringement of Hitachi's patent for static random access memory (SRAM) chips.

Hitachi is seeking to halt sales of Winbond products in the United States, saying they have infringed on Hitachi's patent, and is demanding compensation for damage caused by the alleged infringement, the spokesman said.

Winbond, Taiwan's third-biggest chipmaker, announced early in October that it had slashed its 1996 profit forecast by 54.6 percent to Taiwan $2.3 billion ($83.64 million), the second downward revision in five months.

Winbond said a price war in semiconductor chips was expected to continue into the fourth quarter, but added that a pact with Japan's Toshiba Corp to develop and manufacture leading-edge semiconductor memory products would help the firm's long-term performance.
